abstract.text:
Can any secrets still be shed by that much studied, uniquely integrable,
Elliptic Billiard? Starting by examining the family of 3-periodic trajectories and
the loci of their Triangular Centers, one obtains a beautiful and variegated gallery
of curves: ellipses, quartics, sextics, circles, and even a stationary point. Secondly,
one notices this family conserves an intriguing ratio: Inradius-to-Circumradius. In
turn this implies three conservation corollaries: (i) the sum of bounce angle cosines,
(ii) the product of excentral cosines, and (iii) the ratio of excentral-to-orbit areas.
Monge’s Orthoptic Circle’s close relation to 4-periodic Billiard trajectories is well-known. Its geometry provided clues with which to generalize 3-periodic invariants
to trajectories of an arbitrary number of edges. This was quite unexpected. Indeed,
the Elliptic Billiard did surprise us!

evidence.quote: Indirectly, the Elliptic Billiard did surprise us!

thesis.text: The elliptic billiard still yields surprises: its 3-periodic trajectory family has conserved triangle-center loci and invariants, and these invariants generalize to N-periodic orbits.

sections.summary: The paper frames the elliptic billiard as exhaustively studied yet still surprising, reviews the 3-periodic triangle-center loci, and describes the experimental route from videos and an applet to the conserved r/R ratio and the Monge orthoptic bridge.
sections.title: Introduction and Experimental Motivation

sections.summary: Explains the elliptic billiard as an integrable Hamiltonian system, introduces Joachimsthal's integral, confocal caustics, Poncelet's porism, Monge's orthoptic circle, and the constant gamma and perimeter for periodic families.
sections.title: Integrability, Poncelet Porism, and Monge's Orthoptic Circle

sections.summary: Covers the elliptic loci of major triangle centers X1 through X5, the numerical census of Kimberling centers, and the Excenter locus as a rotated similar ellipse.
sections.title: Elliptic Loci of Major Triangle Centers and Excenters

sections.summary: Surveys derived-triangle loci, the mostly non-elliptic behavior of Intouch, Feuerbach, and Medial triangles, the Extouch and Feuerbach exceptions tied to the caustic and billiard, and the stationary Mittenpunkt X9 with its Circumbilliard corollary.
sections.title: Derived-Triangle Loci, Extouch/Feuerbach, and Stationary Mittenpunkt

sections.summary: Defines the radii r, R, and r9, states the conserved r/R ratio for 3-periodic families, and derives conservation of cosine sum, excentral cosine product, and excentral-to-orbit area ratio.
sections.title: Inradius/Circumradius Conservation and Angle/Area Corollaries

sections.summary: Describes the N=3 circular locus of Q1/Q2 formed by intersections of a tangent with the reflected Excentral Triangle edge, with radius depending on the aspect ratio and always external to the billiard.
sections.title: N=3 Circular Locus

sections.summary: Uses N=4 Monge clues to generalize invariants to N>3: a stationary generalized Mittenpunkt, Tangential Polygon perpendicular feet sweeping the caustic, and conserved cosine sum and product.
sections.title: Generalizing to N>3: Stationary Point, Extouchpoints, Cosine Invariants

sections.summary: Shows that the tangential-to-orbit area ratio is conserved only for odd N and generalizes the N>4 circular locus to intersections of tangential edges reflected about the billiard center, with radius 1/gamma.
sections.title: N>3 Area Ratio and N>4 Circular Loci

sections.summary: Lists open questions about elliptic versus complicated loci, three-dimensional counterparts, self-intersecting orbits, non-billiard Poncelet families, spherical and ellipsoidal billiards, and expressions for tangential product and area ratios.
sections.title: Conclusion and Open Questions

sections.summary: Navigation unit for the video quick-reference table, the postscript on recent proofs, acknowledgements, and the bibliography.
sections.title: Video Index, Acknowledgments, and References

type.reason: It presents new mathematical results (theorems, corollaries, proofs) about elliptic billiard invariants rather than reviewing existing literature.

abstract.text:
Can any secrets still be shed by that much studied, uniquely integrable,
Elliptic Billiard? Starting by examining the family of 3-periodic trajectories and
the loci of their Triangular Centers, one obtains a beautiful and variegated gallery
of curves: ellipses, quartics, sextics, circles, and even a stationary point. Secondly,
one notices this family conserves an intriguing ratio: Inradius-to-Circumradius. In
turn this implies three conservation corollaries: (i) the sum of bounce angle cosines,
(ii) the product of excentral cosines, and (iii) the ratio of excentral-to-orbit areas.
Monge’s Orthoptic Circle’s close relation to 4-periodic Billiard trajectories is well-known. Its geometry provided clues with which to generalize 3-periodic invariants
to trajectories of an arbitrary number of edges. This was quite unexpected. Indeed,
the Elliptic Billiard did surprise us!

evidence.quote: Indeed, the Elliptic Billiard did surprise us!

thesis.text: The elliptic billiard still yields surprises: its 3-periodic trajectory family has conserved triangle-center loci and invariants, and these invariants generalize to N-periodic orbits.

sections.summary: The paper frames the elliptic billiard as exhaustively studied yet still surprising, reviews the 3-periodic triangle-center loci, and describes the experimental route from videos and an applet to the conserved r/R ratio and the Monge orthoptic bridge.
sections.title: Introduction and Experimental Motivation

sections.summary: Explains the elliptic billiard as an integrable Hamiltonian system, introduces Joachimsthal's integral, confocal caustics, Poncelet's porism, Monge's orthoptic circle, and the constant gamma and perimeter for periodic families.
sections.title: Integrability, Poncelet Porism, and Monge's Orthoptic Circle

sections.summary: Covers the elliptic loci of major triangle centers X1 through X5, the numerical census of Kimberling centers, and the Excenter locus as a rotated similar ellipse.
sections.title: Elliptic Loci of Major Triangle Centers and Excenters

sections.summary: Surveys derived-triangle loci, the mostly non-elliptic behavior of Intouch, Feuerbach, and Medial triangles, the Extouch and Feuerbach exceptions tied to the caustic and billiard, and the stationary Mittenpunkt X9 with its Circumbilliard corollary.
sections.title: Derived-Triangle Loci, Extouch/Feuerbach, and Stationary Mittenpunkt

sections.summary: Defines the radii r, R, and r9, states the conserved r/R ratio for 3-periodic families, and derives conservation of cosine sum, excentral cosine product, and excentral-to-orbit area ratio.
sections.title: Inradius/Circumradius Conservation and Angle/Area Corollaries

sections.summary: Describes the N=3 circular locus of Q1/Q2 formed by intersections of a tangent with the reflected Excentral Triangle edge, with radius depending on the aspect ratio and always external to the billiard.
sections.title: N=3 Circular Locus

sections.summary: Uses N=4 Monge clues to generalize invariants to N>3: a stationary generalized Mittenpunkt, Tangential Polygon perpendicular feet sweeping the caustic, and conserved cosine sum and product.
sections.title: Generalizing to N>3: Stationary Point, Extouchpoints, Cosine Invariants

sections.summary: Shows that the tangential-to-orbit area ratio is conserved only for odd N and generalizes the N>4 circular locus to intersections of tangential edges reflected about the billiard center, with radius 1/gamma.
sections.title: N>3 Area Ratio and N>4 Circular Loci

sections.summary: Lists open questions about elliptic versus complicated loci, three-dimensional counterparts, self-intersecting orbits, non-billiard Poncelet families, spherical and ellipsoidal billiards, and expressions for tangential product and area ratios.
sections.title: Conclusion and Open Questions

sections.summary: Navigation unit for the video quick-reference table, the postscript on recent proofs, acknowledgements, and the bibliography.
sections.title: Video Index, Acknowledgments, and References
